name: Tapestry LIHTC (The Tapestry)
headline: Gorman & Company and The Colorado Health Foundation are building The Tapestry, a five-story building with 72 family apartments for households earning 30% to 80% AMI plus a ground-floor early learning center and health clinic, on donated land at 1799 N. Pennsylvania St. in Uptown/North Capitol Hill. It won 2025 Round One federal 9%, state and TOC credits from CHFA.
why_it_matters: It shows a health foundation acting as land donor and gap lender: CHF bought a prime infill block, gave it to the deal (valued above $10.8M) and added loans and a parking lease. The deal closed in late 2025 and topped out by August 2026.

status.label: Under construction; vertical framing complete by August 2026
status.detail: The city held a groundbreaking on 2025-12-15 after the financing closed in late 2025. Naked Denver reported on 2026-08-11 that vertical construction was complete and work had moved to the exterior, interiors and building systems. Completion is expected in 2027: the city says late 2027 and Naked Denver says early 2027.

next_step: Watch for a certificate of occupancy and lease-up notice in 2027, and for a CHFA 8609 or placed-in-service listing.

key_numbers.meaning: 8 one-bedroom, 32 two-bedroom, 28 three-bedroom and 4 four-bedroom units at 30% to 80% AMI, with 32 of them three- and four-bedroom.
About $16M over 10 years, plus $650,000 state credit and $93,600 TOC credit.
The budget in Denver's loan agreement is $37,672,332, including $24.65M hard costs and $10 for acquisition, since the land was donated. BusinessDen reported $35M at award.

key_numbers.value: Over $14.5M from The Colorado Health Foundation
key_numbers.meaning: Land valued above $10.8M, a subordinate loan and site preparation, plus a surface parking lease next door, per the applicant.

facts.value: 1799 N. Pennsylvania St., Denver (18th Avenue and Pennsylvania Street, across from CHF headquarters)
CHFA, Gorman and DOLA say Uptown; the city says North Capitol Hill; the application says Uptown/North Capitol Hill
Five stories: one timber podium level and four wood-frame levels, masonry exterior. Average unit sizes are 625, 900, 1,115 and 1,365 sq ft (1BR to 4BR)
Early childhood education center run by Mile High Early Learning, a health clinic run by the Uptown Clinic, and Hope Communities service space; all open to the neighborhood
50 surface spaces (0.69 per unit), plus spaces next door under a 15-year parking lease from CHF
RTD Route 20 about 700 feet away, Civic Center Station 0.5 mile away, and the future East Colfax BRT. Residents get discounted Neighborhood Eco Passes
18th and Penn Building I, LLC, a Wisconsin LLC at Gorman's Oregon, Wisconsin address (Gorman link inferred from the address)
The applicant documents a Denver Housing Authority partnership for a property tax exemption
The former Employers Council property, which CHF bought in 2021

background.text: CHF bought most of the block across from its headquarters in 2021 to build family affordable housing. It ran community outreach with Urban Ventures and, in August 2024, picked Gorman as developer and Hope Communities as services partner.
The TOC narrative says CHF paid a price affordable housing could not afford and then donated the site, valued at more than $10.8M. The city loan budget lists acquisition at $10.
The LIHTC building is one part of a planned Tapestry campus. The application describes a neighboring 100-unit middle-income building.
Zoning was in place and the project had cleared Denver concept review by application time. The team planned to close and start construction in October 2025.
The Phase II found contaminants above EPA levels from historic filling stations and dry cleaning nearby. Remediation is budgeted at $102,000 with a materials management plan.
The market study shows 9.8% vacancy among LIHTC units in the market area and high penetration at 50% and 60% AMI. The applicant sets its 80% AMI rents below the maximum to compete.
There are no homeless set-aside units, Coordinated Entry referrals or project-based vouchers. Rents sit below Denver voucher payment standards, so tenant-based voucher holders can rent.
Parking above the zoning standard triggered a city Transportation Demand Management requirement, met with Eco Pass subsidies and wayfinding.
The city loan covenant spreads every AMI tier across bedroom sizes. For example, the 80% AMI units are 1 one-bedroom, 4 two-bedroom, 8 three-bedroom and 1 four-bedroom, and units float.
Gorman announced the financial closing and construction start in November 2025.

discrepancies.text: Council Resolution CR25-1618, the loan agreement and the 2026 amendment request put the city loan at $2,290,000, while the city's groundbreaking release and Naked Denver say $3.24 million and Bisnow says $3.2M.
The city loan agreement is titled a Linkage Fee loan and Bisnow says linkage fees fund it, while the city's release and the 2026 amendment request name the Affordable Housing Fund as the source.
BusinessDen reported a $35 million construction budget, while the city loan agreement budget totals $37,672,332.
The Denver Gazette and BusinessDen place the project at 17th Avenue and Pennsylvania Street, while CHFA, the application and Naked Denver place it at 1799 N. Pennsylvania St. on 18th Avenue.
What Now names Gorman Architecture as architect, while Naked Denver names SAR+ Architects, and CHFA credits the rendering to Shears Adkins Rockmore Architects.
The city expects completion in late 2027, while Naked Denver says early 2027.
The application narrative cites a walk score of 96, while the TOC narrative cites a Walk Score of 89.

open_questions: Why the city's public figure ($3.24M) differs from the $2,290,000 council-approved loan: a second city loan or a later increase is possible but no record of one was found.
Amounts of the CHF subordinate loan, Raza CMF loan, Vectra Bank debt, NEF equity and equity price.
Whether Robert Wood Johnson Foundation money replaced the Gorman sponsor note.
Terms of the DHA property tax exemption structure and the CHFA LURA affordability period.
Timing and financing of the planned 100-unit middle-income building next door (the 18th and Penn Building II entity name suggests it, but this is not confirmed).
Certificate of occupancy and lease-up dates.
